newsitem.title: INDIA: India industry says Pakistan to buy 500,000T sugar.
newsitem.headline: India industry says Pakistan to buy 500,000T sugar.

text.p: India, the world's largest sugar producer, hopes to export 500,000 tonnes of sugar to Pakistan in the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season, a senior industry official said on Friday.
"We are hoping to do 500,000 tonnes in exports to Pakistan this year," said S.L. Jain, director-general of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA).
Jain told reporters after ISMA's annual general meeting that the Indian sugar industry expected Pakistan, which is faced with a shortage, to import about 700,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97.
He said in 1995/96 Pakistan had bought 400,000 tonnes of sugar out of which 350,000 tonnes were purchased from India. The balance would arrive from Brazil.
Jain said India's sugar export prospects in 1996/97 were bleak since it was undergoing losses in exports due to a fall in world sugar prices and government controls on domestic sugar pricing.
India has exported nearly one million tonnes of sugar in the 1995/96 season.
"The only shade of light is coming from Pakistan. We have an advantage by despatching by rail," Jain said.
